items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: Jonah Jones and Doc Cheatham and Shad Collins were the trumpets.

ctx.x: And I went with Cab. I played baritone in this band, baritone sax. And we had Hilton Jefferson on first and the fellow that used to be with the Blue Rhythm Band. I can never think of his name, on alto with Cab. He used to be with the Blue Rhythm Band, and he's from Chicago. He's been working out -- he just retired from the U.N. here late -- here recently. I can never think of that boy's name, and I knew him for years. Well, anyhow, it was Jeff, him and I was playing

baritone, had Ike Quebec on one tenor and Sam Taylor on the other tenor. Jonah Jones and Doc Cheatham and Shad Collins were the trumpets. And Butch -- I don't know his last name -- he was on one trombone, and Eddie Burke was on the other trombone.

And Milt Hinton, Panama Francis on drums, Milt Hinton on bass and Dave Rivera on piano. And we went down to Uruguay to play for the festival down there, and all of this was involved with trips. So we went down there, and we were down there about eight weeks. We stopped off in Rio, and then we went to Montevideo and stayed there for the duration at the headquarters, and then we went down to Punta del Este, and it was a very marvelous trip, had a great time down there.

items.title: 68728_Jonah
items.q: I brought him in there, because he wasn't working, so I brought him in and I got in front of the band.

ctx.x: And then I was pretty happy there anyway, and making about $50.00 a night tips. In the Vendome Hotel. But now we get back here and then we start to act halfway decent. It was mostly Stuff. I say it was mostly Stuff, because he was the one who had signed everything, you know. Once in California, before we left the first time, he left by himself, and you know what we did? We got Eddie Barefield. Yeah, I'm glad we leaned on it awhile, because I remember. Now, he was out there about a month and a half and he said,…
all right, I hope he stays in New York and we'll keep the band just like this."
